exampleAnswers.title: Integrating the Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
If we let $u=5x,$ then \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=5 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{1}{5}\textrm{d}u = \textrm{d}x. \]

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

$x$ $0$ $\ln 2$
$u$ $0$ $5\ln 2$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\[ \eqalign{ \int_{0}^{\ln 2} 4e^{5x}\, \textrm{d}x &=4\int_{0}^{\ln 2} e^{5x}\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=4\int_{0}^{5\ln 2} e^u \cdot \dfrac{1}{5}\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4}{5}\int_{0}^{\ln\left(2^5\right)} e^u\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4}{5} \cdot e^u \, \bigg|_{0}^{\ln\left(2^5\right)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4}{5} \left(e^{\ln\left(2^5\right)}-e^0\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4}{5}\left(2^5-1\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4}{5}\left(32-1\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4}{5}\cdot 31\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{124}{5}} } \]

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
If we let $u=4x,$ then \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=4 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{1}{4}\textrm{d}u = \textrm{d}x. \]

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

$x$ $0$ $\ln 3$
$u$ $0$ $4\ln 3$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\[ \eqalign{ \int_{0}^{\ln 3} 3e^{4x}\, \textrm{d}x &=3\int_{0}^{\ln 3} e^{4x}\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=3\int_{0}^{4\ln 3} e^u \cdot \dfrac{1}{4}\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{4}\int_{0}^{\ln\left(3^4\right)} e^u\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{4} \cdot e^u \, \bigg|_{0}^{\ln\left(3^4\right)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{4} \left(e^{\ln\left(3^4\right)}-e^0\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{4}\left(3^4-1\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{4}\left(81-1\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{4}\cdot 80\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{60} } \]

example.title: Integrating the Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
If we let $u = -\dfrac{x}{4},$ then \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=-\dfrac{1}{4} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad -4\,\textrm{d}u = \textrm{d}x. \]

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

$x$ $0$ $4$
$u$ $0$ $-1$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\[ \eqalign{ \int_{0}^{4} 5e^{-x/4}\, \textrm{d}x &=5\int_{0}^{4} e^{-x/4}\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=5\int_{0}^{-1} e^u \cdot (-4)\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=-20\int_{0}^{-1} e^u\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=-20 \cdot e^u \, \bigg|_{0}^{-1}\\[5pt] &=-20 \left(e^{-1}-e^0\right)\\[5pt] &=-20\left(e^{-1}-1\right)\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{20-20e^{-1}} } \]

example.title: Integrating the Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.explanation:
If we let $u={2x}$, then \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \dfrac 12{\textrm{d}u}={\textrm{d}x}. \]

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

$x$ $0$ $\ln 5$
$u$ $0$ $2\ln 5$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\[ \eqalign{ \int_{0}^{\ln 5} \dfrac 1 6 e^{2x}\, \textrm{d}x &= \dfrac 1 6\int_{0}^{\ln 5} e^{2x}\,{\textrm{d}x}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 6\int_{0}^{2\ln 5} e^{u}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{12}\int_{0}^{2\ln 5} e^u\,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{12}\Big.\left(e^u\right)\Big|_{0}^{2\ln 5}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{12}\left(e^{2\ln5}-e^0\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{12}\cdot (5^2-1)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{24}{12}\\[5pt] &=2 } \]

example.title: Integrating the Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.explanation:
If we let $u = 5x + 2$, then

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= 5\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac 1 5 \textrm d u = \textrm d x. \]

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ \int \dfrac{e^{5x+2}}{5}\, \textrm{d}x &=\int \dfrac{e^{u}}{5}\cdot \dfrac 1 5 \, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {1}{25} \int e^u \, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & =\dfrac {1}{25} \cdot e^u + C \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {e^{5x+2}}{25} + C } \end{eqnarray}

exampleAnswers.title: Integrating a General Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.explanation:
If we let $u=6x,$ then
\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=6 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \dfrac 16 \, {\textrm{d}u}={\textrm{d}x}. \]

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

$x$ $0$ $1$
$u$ $0$ $6$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\[ \eqalign{ \int_{0}^{1} 3^{6x}\, \textrm{d}x &=\int_{0}^{6} 3^{u}\cdot\dfrac{1}{6}\,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{6}\int_{0}^{6} 3^{u}\,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{6}\Big.\left(\dfrac {3^u}{\ln3}\right)\Bigg|_{0}^{6}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{6\ln3}\left(729- 1 \right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{728}{6\ln3}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{364}{3\ln3} } \]

example.title: Integrating a General Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.explanation:
If we let $u=-2x,$ then
\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=-2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad -\dfrac 12\textrm d u = \textrm d x. \]

Computing our limits of integration,we get the following:

$x$ $0$ $1$
$u$ $0$ $-2$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\[ \eqalign{ \int_{0}^{1} 2^{-2x}\, \textrm{d}x &=\int_{0}^{-2} 2^{u}\,\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{-2} 2^u\,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{2}\Big.\left(\dfrac {2^u}{\ln 2}\right)\Bigg|_{0}^{-2}\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{2\ln2}\left(\dfrac 1 4-1\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{8\ln2} } \]

example.title: Integrating a General Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
If we let $u=x-1,$ then \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u=\textrm{d}x. \]

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

$x$ $0$ $2$
$u$ $-1$ $1$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\[ \eqalign{ \int_{0}^{2} 5^{x-1}\, \textrm{d}x &=\int_{-1}^{1} 5^{u}\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{5^{u}}{\ln 5} \, \Bigg|_{-1}^{1}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{\ln{5}} \left(5^1 - 5^{-1}\right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{\ln 5}\left(5 - \dfrac{1}{5}\right)\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{24}{5\ln 5}} } \]

example.title: Integrating a General Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
If we let $u=6-3x,$ then \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=-3 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad -\dfrac{1}{3}\,\textrm{d}u=\textrm{d}x. \]

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

$x$ $1$ $2$
$u$ $3$ $0$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\[ \eqalign{ \int_{1}^{2} 2\cdot 3^{6-3x}\, \textrm{d}x &=\int_{3}^{0} 2\cdot 3^{u}\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{2}{3}\int_{3}^{0} 3^{u}\,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{2}{3} \left(\dfrac{3^{u}}{\ln 3}\right) \Bigg|_{3}^{0}\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{2}{3\ln{3}} \left(3^0 - 3^3\right)\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{2}{3\ln 3}\left(1 - 27\right)\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{52}{3\ln 3}} } \]

example.title: Integrating a General Exponential Function With a Linear Exponent

question.explanation:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=4x+6.$ Differentiating gives \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=4 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm d u = 4\, \textrm d x. \]

and therefore

\[ \eqalign{ \int 8\cdot 2^{4x+6}\, \textrm{d}x &=\int 2\cdot 2^{4x+6}\cdot 4 \,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=2\int 2^{u}\,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac {2\cdot 2^u}{\ln 2} + C\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2\cdot 2^{4x+6}}{\ln 2} + C\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2^{4x+7}}{\ln 2} + C } \]
